info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description:
The webhook and audit subscriptions that are not deleted, newest first, one-based pages,
optionally only one kind or only active ones. Integration administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

post.description:
A webhook or audit subscription: which entities, operations and named events it matches, the
target URL (http or https, screened against private addresses now and at every send), retry class,
payload shape and owner. The signing secret is generated here and returned once, in the plain and
the Standard Webhooks form; it is stored encrypted. Integration administrators only. Audited.

get.description: One subscription's settings and filters, without its secret. Integration administrators only.

delete.description:
Marks the subscription deleted and inactive, so it matches nothing more; its delivery log stays.
Integration administrators only. Audited.

patch.description:
Changes the fields given (name, active, filters, target URL, retry class, attempts, payload
shape, target authentication) when `row_version` is the stored one; a stale version is 409.
Integration administrators only. Audited.

get.description:
The delivery log of one subscription, newest first, one-based pages, optionally only one status:
attempts, the last error and HTTP status, and when it was delivered. Integration administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

post.description: Sends again every delivery the subscription matched since `from` (M13-T4): delivered, failed and dead-lettered ones go back to pending with their attempts reset, at most 10,000. Each keeps its event id, so a receiver that deduplicates on `webhook-id` sees a retry, not a new event.

Generates a new signing secret, stores it encrypted and returns it once; deliveries are signed
with it from now on. Integration administrators only. Audited as a credential rotation.
Queues one test delivery to the subscription's target (M13-T4): entity `attome_test`, operation `test`, signed like every delivery. Its outcome shows in the delivery log.

An outside system with its base URL, screened against private addresses, and optionally its
credential, stored encrypted before the system is readable. Listing, renaming and deleting stay on
the record API. Integration administrators only. Audited.

Stores a new credential for the system, encrypted; it is never returned. Integration administrators
only. Audited.

Calls the system's health check, guarded against private addresses when it dials. Integration
administrators only.

get.description:
P13-T2: the script that loads one entity's warehouse export into
Snowflake or BigQuery, to schedule on the warehouse side (a Snowflake
task, a BigQuery scheduled query). It stages the new files, keeps each
record's newest change and merges by `id`, deleting tombstones.
Administrators only; Attome holds no warehouse credentials.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Snowflake: the external stage over the export's bucket.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: BigQuery: the bucket the export writes to, `gs://bucket[/prefix]`.

422.description: A missing or unusable stage, dataset or bucket

get.summary: Get the Microsoft admin consent URL
get.description: The URL a Microsoft tenant's administrator opens to consent to mail sync for every person at once.

post.description:
Where an outside system posts its events, with no session: the call must carry a timestamp within
five minutes and an HMAC-SHA256 signature with the system's credential over the timestamp and the
raw body.

parameters.name: x-integration-timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds; must be within ±300 s of server time

parameters.name: x-integration-signature
parameters.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 with the system's credential over "{x-integration-timestamp}.{raw body}"

401.description: Missing or invalid signature, or a missing, malformed or stale timestamp

404.description: No such system, or this module is not licensed

409.description: Replay: this signed request was already accepted

503.description: The replay-protection store is unavailable; retry later

get.description:
The caller's mailbox connections: at most one per provider, so the whole
list is one page.

delete.description: Disconnects: revokes at the provider where it can, then forgets the tokens.

404.description: No such connection of the caller's

get.description:
Where the provider sends the person back; keeps the tokens and returns
them to their settings page.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: The mail provider the connection is for

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code the provider sent back.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state value this sign-in started with.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The error the provider sent back, if any.

404.description: No such sign-in of the caller's

post.description: Starts connecting: answers the provider's sign-in URL.

x-audit-exempt.note: keeps a ten-minute PKCE verifier; the connection and its Credential event are made at the callback

post.description: J7-T1: creates an online meeting with its join link.

422.description: Bad times or subject, no connected account, or the provider refused

x-audit-exempt.note: creates the meeting at the provider; nothing is stored in Attome until the caller saves it on a record

get.description: J7-T1: who attended and the recordings, after the meeting.

post.description:
A provider's delivery receipt for one message; the token names the message, and a bad or expired
one, or a receipt for another provider message, is 404. No session.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The receipt token sent with the message

422.description: Not a receipt this route reads

x-audit-exempt.note: a provider's delivery receipt moving one SMS ledger row forward; no business or security effect

Attendee.description: One person's time in a meeting.

external_system.description:
L1-T7: the system this subscriber is, as master-data contributions
name it; a golden-record change then carries its own external id.

filter_event_names.description:
Matches a named change-feed event (`attome_core::change_feed::
emit_named`, e.g. `"sla.breached"`) — migration `0441`,
REVIEW-2026-09-02 finding #3. An unnamed (ordinary) event never
matches a non-null list here.

filter_expression.description:
Reserved for M45 (attome-rules) — stored, never evaluated in Phase 1.
See `attome_events::filter`'s module doc.

ordered.description: M13-T3: send one record's events one at a time, in order.

payload_shape.description:
M13-T1: `id`, `changes` or `full` (the default): what each webhook
body carries besides the entity, record id and operation.

target_auth_header.description:
M13-T2: a header the target wants on every delivery, e.g.
`Authorization`; its value is write-only.

config.description:
JSON-encoded adapter config (endpoint templates, pagination style) —
stored as-is; `connector::adapters::rest` reads it once Phase 2 needs
per-system endpoint shaping.

credential_value.description:
Plaintext, accepted exactly once — never stored on the entity row,
never echoed back. Optional: a system can be registered before its
credential is known and rotated in later.

service_principal_ref.description:
The `user_account` id whose `SecurityContext` gates every
write this system's inbound webhook makes (D-425) — see
`system::ensure_service_principal_exists`.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

PaginatedResponse_DeliveryListItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_MailConnection.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: A connection, as its owner sees it.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_SubscriptionListItem.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

QueuedDeliveries.description: M13-T4: what a test send or a replay queued.

delivery_id.description: The test delivery's id (test send only).

from.description: Every delivery matched at or after this time is sent again.

is_set.description: Q18-T6: a credential is stored; no part of it is returned.

updated_at.description: When the stored credential was set.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

webhook_secret_standard.description: M13-T2: the new secret in Standard Webhooks form. Shown once.

SubscriptionCreatedResponse.description:
Same shape as `attome-s2s`'s `KeyCreatedResponse` — the plaintext secret is
returned exactly once, at creation/rotation time, and never again (M62
plan §5: "Secrets never returned by the API after creation, same as S2S
keys").

webhook_secret_standard.description:
M13-T2: the same secret as a Standard Webhooks verifier takes it
(`whsec_…`), for the `webhook-signature` header. Shown once.

external_system.description: L1-T7: the system this subscriber is, for its own external ids.

ordered.description: M13-T3: one record's events are sent one at a time, in order.

paused_at.description: M13-T3: when and why the endpoint's failures turned it off.

target_auth_header.description: M13-T2: the target auth header's name; its value is never returned.

target_url.description:
Never the secret — see `secret_rotate`'s response for the one place a
plaintext secret is ever returned.

credential_configured.description:
Whether `credential_value` was provided and stored — never the value
itself.

external_system.description: L1-T7: omitting it keeps the current one; an empty one removes it.

filter_entity_logicalnames.description:
Omitting the field keeps the current filter; providing one (`[]` for
"match nothing" or a non-empty list) replaces it wholesale. Phase 1
has no way to PATCH a filter back to NULL ("match everything") short
of deleting and recreating the subscription — a narrower surface than
double-`Option` JSON semantics would give, deliberately: serde's
default `Option<Option<T>>` handling cannot distinguish an absent key
from an explicit `null` without a custom deserializer this crate
doesn't carry, and a silently-wrong distinction here is worse than a
missing feature.

filter_event_names.description:
Same replace-wholesale-or-omit convention as the two filters above —
see this struct's doc comment. Migration `0441`.

ordered.description: M13-T3: omitting it keeps the current one.

payload_shape.description: M13-T1: `id`, `changes` or `full`; omitting it keeps the current one.

target_auth_header.description:
M13-T2: replaces the target's auth header (name and value together);
an empty name removes it; omitting both keeps it.

Warehouse.description: The warehouse a script is for.

schema_version.description: The export's schema version the script was written for.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
